notes:
Bit field, bit extender, uneven pieces, more bus widths

A RISC-V instruction keeps its fields at odd places (rd in bits 11..7,
immediates scattered over several fields) and widens 12-bit numbers
with their sign. New parts: the bit field takes neighbouring bits out
of a bus, the bit extender widens with zeros or the sign; splitter and
combiner take a list of uneven pieces. Buses may now also be 3, 5, 6,
7, 12, 20 and 24 bits wide, and a program memory can hold a plain
table (for control units).
